devdoc.details: This contract implements a proxy that is upgradeable by an admin.  To avoid https://medium.com/nomic-labs-blog/malicious-backdoors-in-ethereum-proxies-62629adf3357[proxy selector clashing], which can potentially be used in an attack, this contract uses the https://blog.openzeppelin.com/the-transparent-proxy-pattern/[transparent proxy pattern]. This pattern implies two things that go hand in hand:  1. If any account other than the admin calls the proxy, the call will be forwarded to the implementation, even if that call matches one of the admin functions exposed by the proxy itself. 2. If the admin calls the proxy, it can access the admin functions, but its calls will never be forwarded to the implementation. If the admin tries to call a function on the implementation it will fail with an error that says "admin cannot fallback to proxy target".  These properties mean that the admin account can only be used for admin actions like upgrading the proxy or changing the admin, so it's best if it's a dedicated account that is not used for anything else. This will avoid headaches due to sudden errors when trying to call a function from the proxy implementation.  Our recommendation is for the dedicated account to be an instance of the {ProxyAdmin} contract. If set up this way, you should think of the `ProxyAdmin` instance as the real administrative inerface of your proxy.

explanation: Static implementation/source inventory with dated read-only proxy/dependency observations, not future runtime identity, liquidity, financial-safety or execution assurance. Calls require zero native value and existing grants, canonical calldata, allowances, balances and independent controls.

Ethereum TellerV2 is the transparent proxy 0x00182FdB0B880eE24D428e3Cc39383717677C37e; applicable reported implementation is 0x37F483C895C66d3eDb14AE88ea9bA52F937Eb002, not constructor initial logic. Upgrade, market registry, collateral escrow, lender manager, pausing manager and reputation dependencies remain authoritative.

Principal and repayment amounts use each loan ERC20 lending-token raw units (not universally USDC); WETH stays ERC20, no native wrapping. APR is basis points (10000=100%). Duration is seconds; market-selected payment cycle, payment type, default period and bid expiration are captured per bid. Integer divisions round down; interest accrues using 360-day year for Monthly and 365 days for Seconds.

submitBid only records a pending loan request and optional collateral commitment, not guaranteed funding. Borrower must be market-verified and market open. Metadata URI is stored and hashed, not executed. Receiver zero resolves to borrower. Lender acceptance requires verified lender, nonclosed market, unexpired pending bid, lender principal allowance to TellerV2 and any borrower collateral allowances to CollateralManager.

Collateral tuple is (enum type, amount, tokenId, tokenAddress), supporting ERC20/ERC721/ERC1155, not arbitrary target+payload. Submitting collateral checks balances/ownership and records it; acceptance pulls collateral into escrow. ERC721 amount must be one; positive amounts are required when funding. Market borrower/lender verification may impose KYC, allowlists or jurisdiction eligibility; catalog access cannot satisfy those conditions.

Acceptance deducts protocol and marketplace fees from principal before receiver proceeds; both are basis-point floor divisions. Observed protocol fee was 5 bps at the recorded block, not a guaranteed future setting. Fee-on-transfer lending tokens are rejected by the exact receiver-balance-delta check. No max-fee, minimum net proceeds or caller deadline argument is supplied.

Repayment can be funded by any caller, not solely borrower, and pulls that caller lending tokens using allowance to TellerV2. Full/minimum amounts are computed at transaction time. Custom repay amount must cover minimum principal due plus interest. Do not overpay: _repayLoan caps only its local paymentAmount, while cumulative principal and _sendOrEscrowFunds still use the original Payment struct, so excess can be transferred/accounted rather than refunded.

Normal full repayment marks PAID and calls configured collateral manager withdrawal to the recorded borrower (not payer or lender). WithoutCollateralWithdraw variants leave collateral escrowed for a separate manager withdrawal not admitted here. Collateral-manager pause or transfer restrictions can revert normal full repayment; without-withdraw variants do not promise successful execution.

Repayment first attempts transferFrom to current lender (NFT owner after claimLoanNFT); failure routes funds via configured escrow vault for lender. A loan-specific lender-set repayment listener receives only fixed repayLoanCallback(bidId,payer,principal,interest) at zero native value and capped gas; callback failure is ignored but minimum gas check can revert. This is not caller-supplied arbitrary callback calldata or a callback setter capability.

claimLoanNFT requires the recorded direct lender and an accepted loan; it registers the loan with lender manager and makes NFT ownership determine future lender. No NFT transfer/approval, forwarder authorization, listener setter, arbitrary executor, liquidation or admin capability is admitted. Direct smart-wallet calls use their own caller identity; ERC2771 and market forwarder suffix identities do not grant impersonation through canonical catalog calls.

submitBid, lenderAcceptBid and claimLoanNFT require protocol unpaused. Cancellation and repayment do not have that top-level modifier, but dependencies can still pause/revert. Loan funds are committed for loan terms; this is direct loan-book funding, not an instantly redeemable pooled vault. Source says borrower receives collateral; an older withdraw documentation sentence saying lender is not substituted for actual implementation.
documentationDiscrepancies: Old uncollateralized submitBid docs include paymentCycle and bytes32 metadata not in applicable ABI; actual implementation string URI ABI used.
Withdraw guide says lender; actual manager withdraw uses tellerV2.getLoanBorrower, so source wins.
_repayLoan local paymentAmount cap does not cap original Payment struct passed to accounting and transfer.
